analysis.reading:
THE PRIMARY SOURCE ARRIVES AND THE INTERVENTION DOES NOT. Card 4 is the MARXISTS INTERNET ARCHIVE hosting two English editions of the 1844 Manuscripts — the actual text the Phase X reconstruction addresses — and card 5 insists "it is necessary to go back to the ORIGINAL TEXT and delve deeper step by step according to Marx’s narrative order", which is precisely the philological method the reconstruction claims to use.

Three ways of reading Phase X now sit in the corpus from three captures of nearly the same query. On 14 June «phase x completion of marx» cited the Zenodo deposit INLINE while its cards were popular Marx scholarship. On 17 June «"Phase X" Marx 1844» composed it as "modern theoretical philosophy" with no author. Here, «"Phase X" Marx 1844 alienation», the third term pulls the query fully into the established literature and the archive vanishes from both answer and sourcing.

Adding a real scholarly term to a query containing a coinage moved the whole query into the field that owns the real term.

atoms.evidence: the term "Phase X" does not originate from Marx’s writings
used to describe the unwritten transition in Marx's early work
"Phase X" refers to the lingering symbolic and linguistic alienation that remains even after material or economic structures (the base) have been changed.
It is a concept from modern theoretical philosophy used to describe the unwritten transition in Marx's early work between abolishing material alienation and restructuring human thought.
